rules: Species visual profile defines biology/morphology only; it does not define culture, organization, clothing or personality.
Canonical morphology evidence is required before locking unsupported details.
Individual variation is required within canon-compatible bounds.
Persistent characters preserve their individual morphology across all assets.
Major-species production must resolve through the individual profile catalog rather than relying only on framework-level observations.

visual_rules: Human is a biological baseline only.
Do not infer Earth upbringing, Federation citizenship or Starfleet membership.
Morphology must follow validated Vulcan visual references.
Logical discipline is not a visual personality stereotype.
Do not use uniform or culture to substitute for species identity.
Two antennae are persistent anatomical identity features unless explicit injury/state changes them.
Antenna injury/regrowth must evolve the same individual's visual identity.
Morphology requires validated source/reference profile before production lock.
Argumentative cultural norms must not be encoded as permanent facial aggression.
Do not make warrior equipment or aggressive pose a species default.

visual_cues: blue-to-cyan skin presentation with meaningful individual/production variation
paired cranial antennae as primary species-readability feature
antenna angle, curvature, length and presentation may vary by individual/reference
white-to-silver hair is a strong recurring visual association in the supplied references
humanlike facial individuality remains broad beneath species traits
guardrails: Do not force one exact shade of blue on every Andorian.
Do not use aggressive expression or martial styling as a species default.
Antennae belong to persistent individual morphology and must remain recognizable across later images.

visual_cues: strongly non-human nasal/snout morphology
large and highly distinctive ear structures
pronounced brow and mid-face sculpting
facial hair can be visually prominent in some references but must not become universal
significant morphology/presentation variation exists across production eras
guardrails: Do not reduce Tellarites to a single prosthetic face template.
Era-specific visual interpretation must be resolved before production lock.
Argumentative cultural norms must not be encoded as permanent angry facial expression.

visual_cues: pointed external ears as the strongest persistent species marker
upswept or strongly angled eyebrow presentation is a recurring screen cue
otherwise broad humanlike facial variation is present
haircut and grooming vary and are not biological identity
skin tone remains within broad humanlike variation in the supplied references
guardrails: Do not treat a specific bowl-style haircut as a biological species trait.
Do not encode emotional restraint as a permanently blank face.
Ear shape must stay consistent for a persistent individual across images.

visual_cues: very large external ears are a dominant species-readability feature
pronounced cranial/forehead ridge structure
distinctive nasal bridge and central facial anatomy
strong individual variation remains visible despite shared species morphology
clothing and commercial styling are cultural/occupational layers, not species anatomy
guardrails: Do not infer merchant profession, greed or personality from Ferengi morphology.
Ear and cranial structure belong to persistent individual morphology.
Do not make every Ferengi face identical by overusing one prosthetic pattern.

visual_cues: cranial and facial ridge architecture is the dominant species-readability feature
central forehead structure and temple/eye-region ridges vary meaningfully by individual
ridge continuity can extend from head through jaw and neck
neck surface patterning and relief are prominent recurring anatomical cues
skin presentation ranges through pale grey, beige and brown-grey tones in the supplied references
hair remains an individual presentation layer and is not part of the cranial ridge identity
guardrails: Do not use one prosthetic ridge map as the template for all Cardassians.
Cranial, facial and neck ridge topology belongs to persistent individual morphology.
Do not infer political loyalty, military role or personality from Cardassian anatomy.
Sex/gender presentation must not be reduced to a single cranial-ridge pattern without validated canon support.

visual_cues: forehead cranial ridges are the primary recurring species-readability feature in the supplied late-24th-century-style references
ridge geometry varies strongly between individuals rather than following one universal pattern
cranial structure can influence forehead height, brow silhouette and upper-face contour
humanlike variation in skin tone, hair, facial proportions and facial hair remains broad
female and male-presenting individuals both retain strong cranial-ridge individuality
hair length and styling are presentation choices rather than species anatomy
guardrails: Do not clone a single famous Klingon ridge pattern across procedural NPCs.
Do not encode aggression, warrior profession or honor stance into neutral facial expression.
Forehead-ridge topology is part of persistent visual identity and must survive age/state changes.
Era-aware morphology rules are required before production locking because Klingon screen presentation changes across periods.

visual_cues: asymmetrical cybernetic augmentation can alter face, skull, eye region, torso and limbs while leaving portions of origin-species anatomy visible
ocular implants, cranial housings, cabling, tubes, armor-like components and dermal pallor are recurring cues
implant coverage and arrangement may vary significantly by drone/function/individual
origin facial structure can remain partially recognizable beneath assimilation hardware
assimilation presentation may range from partial facial/cranial augmentation to extensive full-body drone configuration
guardrails: Never replace origin_species_id with a fictional Borg species identity.
Assimilation overlays and modifies an existing persistent visual identity; it does not reroll the person.
Liberation/removal of implants must evolve from the same identity/history rather than generate a new face.
Implant layout must not grant memories, authority, personality or knowledge.
Cybernetic components require state/function provenance; do not add random implants purely for visual drama.
